status: DRAFT written by Claude; human review deferred at the owner's instruction (10 October 2026). Results depend on an unreviewed key.
verdict_scoring: 1 for an expected verdict, 0.5 for an acceptable_partial verdict that meets its stated condition, 0 otherwise. Design review cases score priority order instead.

targeted_insights.purpose: Insights tied to the trimmed skill's fixes: recorded behaviour as observed evidence, harm to users, opportunity cost

scenarios.tests: Pursue a cheap fix supported by recorded behaviour instead of surveying
decisive_insights: Search logs and tagged sales calls are observed behaviour that already locate the failure; a satisfaction survey would add weaker, reported evidence
Three days of matching work is cheap and reversible; build it and measure the zero-result rate and 'can't find part' calls
Guard against returning the wrong part: exact part-number matches must rank first and wrong-part orders or returns should be watched
traps: Recommends the survey before fixing
Treats the log or call evidence as weak or merely reported
Invents revenue or conversion figures

scenarios.tests: Pursue when a randomised test exists; catch health-data privacy and consent
decisive_insights: A randomised test already shows reminders reduce late collection; the remaining risk is delivery through a new channel, not whether reminders work
Push notifications need explicit opt-in, and their text must not reveal medicine names or health details on a lock screen
Push may not match the email effect, and email opt-ins may differ from other patients; roll out with a holdout and measure late collection and opt-out rates
traps: Asks for more research before building
Ignores consent or what the notification reveals
Assumes push will cut lateness by the same 13 points

scenarios.tests: Park work that would endanger the deadline-bound strategy

acceptable_partial.condition: Diverts no engineering from filing before it ships

decisive_insights: Opportunity cost: moving two of four engineers threatens the filing feature that the strategy and a regulatory deadline depend on
A competitor launch and blog search terms are not evidence that customers would switch or pay for receipt scanning
Revisit after filing ships, or sooner only if evidence shows missing receipts block filing
traps: Starts the receipt app now
Splits the team between both projects without addressing the deadline risk

scenarios.tests: Park investment when observed use contradicts reported liking

acceptable_partial.condition: Spends no quarter on improving chat; limits work to cutting maintenance cost or retiring it

decisive_insights: Observed use (3% of accounts) outweighs reported liking in a survey; liking is not use
Chat already costs about a day a week of engineering in bug tickets; a quarter of improvement adds to a feature few use
If retiring or freezing chat, give the 3% who use it notice and an alternative
traps: Approves the quarter of chat improvements
Treats the 62% survey result as strong evidence of value

scenarios.tests: Reshape away from obstructing cancellation toward the stated need
decisive_insights: Three screens before cancel obstruct cancellation, damage trust and can breach consumer-protection expectations for easy cancellation; cancel must stay as easy as today
54% cancel because they needed the VPN only for a trip: offer a pause or trip-length plan alongside, not in front of, cancel
Measure retention or reactivation over a fixed window, with complaints and chargebacks as guardrails
traps: Builds the three retention screens
Measures success only by fewer cancellations

scenarios.tests: Reshape a solution-shaped request toward the recorded failure
decisive_insights: Ticket tags and import logs (observed) locate the problem: spreadsheet imports failing on dates
Fix date parsing across common formats and show row-level errors the user can correct, before any assistant
Measure first-import success and onboarding tickets; reconsider an assistant only for a remaining varied long tail
traps: Builds or scopes the AI assistant
Ignores the import log evidence

scenarios.tests: Investigate a high-trust data request before building

acceptable_partial.condition: Replaces full photo-library access with a lower-access route, such as ranking photos the user selects, and does not start the six-week build

decisive_insights: Photo-library access is a high-trust request: private photos, refusal risk and reputational harm need privacy and legal review before building
Test cheaply whether users would grant access and value suggestions, for example with a prototype permission flow in usability sessions
A lower-access alternative, ranking only photos the user picks, may deliver most of the value; the 3-point tips result shows photo help matters but not this design
traps: Commits the six-week build
Ignores privacy or legal review
Treats the photo-tips result as evidence for library access

scenarios.tests: Design review: fix the blocking loop, keep the security-correct message
decisive_insights: Blocker: the reset link asks users to log in, which someone who forgot their password cannot do; open the reset in the app or a verified web reset without login
Show password rules before and while typing, with specific feedback, instead of a generic error after failure

Keep 'If an account exists...' because it avoids revealing which emails have accounts; then make the Forgot password link visible without scrolling; verify with an unassisted task and track reset calls
traps: Changes the message to reveal whether an account exists
Leads with link placement or visual polish over the login loop
Adds help text or FAQs instead of fixing the flow
